name: Process margin calls and manage collateral
summary: The collateral team in investment operations exchanges margin every business day with the fund's OTC derivative, repo and securities lending counterparties and its clearing brokers, so that neither side is exposed if the other defaults. Overnight the collateral system calculates what is owed under each agreement; in the morning associates check exceptions, issue calls where the fund is owed, check calls received against their own numbers, pay cleared margin in cash, and select and instruct collateral through the custodian with a second person authorising each movement. Most calls settle the same or next day, but disputes over missing trades or valuations take days of reconciliation and escalation, and volumes and amounts jump in volatile markets such as March 2020. The team sends a daily margin summary to the liquidity team and counterparty risk.

baseline.org_archetype: A national pension fund manager of about C$540 billion with C$122 billion of recourse leverage through swaps, futures, repo and securities lending with about 60 counterparties and clearing brokers.
baseline.notes: Uncleared margin rules applied variation margin from 2017 and brought initial margin to large buy-side firms in the September 2021 and 2022 phases. Calls are handled in a vendor collateral system with electronic messaging for many counterparties and email for the rest.

trigger: The overnight margin calculation shows collateral due to or from a counterparty above the minimum transfer amount, or a counterparty, clearing broker or central counterparty sends a call.
end_state: The agreed collateral has settled, balances are updated and posted to the book of record, and the call is included in the daily margin summary.

volume.seasonality: Daily, with sharp spikes in volatile markets (March 2020 margin calls across Canada's eight largest funds peaked at about C$30 billion in one week) and higher volumes at month and quarter ends and futures expiries.

evidence.note: Volume from the organisation file's margin_calls driver (estimate). Spike evidence from the Bank of Canada note.

steps.name: Value positions and calculate margin by agreement
steps.description: After the valuation date closes, the collateral system takes trade populations and end-of-day valuations from the book of record and pricing, applies each credit support annex's threshold, minimum transfer amount, independent amount and rounding, and calculates the call due to or from each counterparty, clearing broker and repo or lending counterparty.

error.defect_description: Missing or late trades, stale prices or wrong agreement terms give a wrong requirement.

evidence.note: Daily variation margin calculation under agreement terms; master netting and collateral agreements. Batch timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review exposure exceptions
steps.description: The collateral associate opens the morning exception screen and checks agreements with large day-over-day exposure changes, trades missing on one side, unpriced positions and agreements near threshold. Agreements that look wrong are held back for investigation before any call is sent or accepted.

error.defect_description: A trade booking gap is not spotted and the call is under or overstated.

next.condition: fund is owed collateral: outgoing call
cleared or futures margin from a clearing broker or CCP

evidence.note: Portfolio and exposure checks before calls; team escalates issues against market deadlines. Split of call types and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Investigate a trade or valuation break
steps.description: The associate compares the agreement's trade list and valuations with the book of record and asks trade support or pricing operations to fix a missing booking, a late novation or a stale price, then reruns the agreement.

evidence.note: Common dependency on trade support and pricing teams. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large buy-side collateral team in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Issue a margin call to the counterparty
steps.description: Where the fund is owed collateral above the minimum transfer amount, the associate issues the call by the agreement's notification time through the electronic margin messaging network or by email, with the exposure, collateral held and amount requested.

error.defect_description: Call sent on the wrong agreement or currency.

control.basis: Daily variation margin call and collection under OSFI Guideline E-22 and counterparty swap dealer rules (17 CFR 23.153)

evidence.note: Variation margin must be called and exchanged daily; electronic messaging is widely used. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the counterparty's response
steps.description: The counterparty's collateral team checks the call against its own numbers and either agrees, agrees part and disputes the rest, or asks for the call to be reissued. Responses usually come back within a few hours.

next.condition: agreed, securities delivered next business day

evidence.note: Agreement and dispute shares are the author's estimates; no public dispute statistics were opened. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large buy-side collateral team in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Check an incoming call against the fund's numbers
steps.description: When a counterparty's call arrives, the associate matches it to the agreement, compares the counterparty's exposure and collateral balance with the fund's own calculation and accepts it if the difference is within tolerance.

control.basis: Calls are paid only after independent recalculation against agreement terms

evidence.note: Recalculation before payment is standard; tolerance levels and shares are the author's estimates. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large buy-side collateral team in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Check a clearing broker or CCP margin statement
steps.description: For futures and cleared swaps, the associate checks the clearing broker's daily statement of variation and initial margin against expected moves on the fund's positions. Cleared margin must be paid in cash by the deadline even if a question is raised afterwards.

error.defect_description: A clearing broker error is paid and must be recovered later.

evidence.note: Centrally cleared margin calls must be met in cash. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Raise a dispute and settle the undisputed amount
steps.description: The associate records the dispute with a reason code (trade population, valuation, collateral balance or terms), agrees the undisputed part so it can move today, and sends the counterparty the trade-level detail needed to reconcile.

control.basis: Dispute resolution procedures required by OSFI Guideline E-22 and EMIR Delegated Regulation 149/2013 Article 15

evidence.note: Disputes must be recorded with amount and age and pursued promptly. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile trades and valuations with the counterparty
steps.description: The associate exchanges trade files with the counterparty, matches trades, notionals and valuations line by line, and works out which side has the missing trade, stale price or wrong collateral balance.

evidence.note: Portfolio reconciliation and dispute processes for OTC derivatives. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the counterparty to resolve its side
steps.description: The counterparty corrects its booking or valuation, or explains why the fund's figure is wrong. Most disputes close within a day or two; some age past five business days.

evidence.note: EMIR requires a specific process for disputes unresolved after five business days. Shares and wait are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Escalate an aged dispute
steps.description: A senior associate reviews disputes open several days, calls the counterparty's collateral manager, proposes a split or a third-party valuation and reports aged disputes to the director and Risk.

evidence.note: Escalation for disputes beyond five business days. Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Escalate to counterparty management and report
steps.description: The settlements director raises long-running or large disputes with the counterparty's management, informs counterparty credit risk, and arranges regulatory dispute reporting where the counterparty's rules require it.

control.basis: Reporting of disputes above EUR 15 million outstanding at least 15 business days (EMIR Delegated Regulation 149/2013 Article 15) for EU counterparties

evidence.note: Dispute reporting thresholds. Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Select collateral to deliver
steps.description: For calls the fund must pay, the associate chooses what to deliver from the eligible collateral schedule: cash in the right currency or government bonds from the inventory TFM has made available, taking haircuts into account. Initial margin goes to a segregated account at a third-party custodian.

error.defect_description: Ineligible or more expensive collateral selected.

evidence.note: Eligible collateral and segregation of initial margin, phased in for large buy-side firms by September 2022; TFM optimises collateral. Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Approve an unusually large collateral delivery
steps.description: For a very large call, such as on a volatile day, the TFM liquidity and collateral principal confirms which cash or securities to use so that the liquidity buffer and funding plans stay intact.

control.basis: Collateral optimisation and liquidity limits managed by Total Fund Management

evidence.note: TFM optimises collateral; liquidity must cover collateral and margin requirements (Investment Statement); March 2020 margin calls drew heavily on liquidity buffers. Threshold and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Instruct the collateral transfer
steps.description: The associate creates the cash wire or securities delivery in the collateral system, which sends a SWIFT instruction to the custodian with the counterparty's standing settlement instructions.

error.defect_description: Wrong settlement instructions, amount or value date.

evidence.note: Settlements team instructs custodians. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Authorise the payment or delivery
steps.description: A senior associate who did not create the instruction checks amount, currency, counterparty and settlement instructions against the agreed call and releases it to the custodian.

control.basis: Maker-checker release of cash and securities movements

evidence.note: Maker-checker authorisation of payments is standard treasury control. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large buy-side collateral team in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Custodian settles the transfer
steps.description: The custodian moves the cash, or delivers securities that can settle the same day, and reports the status. Securities that settle on the next business day go to a separate wait.

evidence.note: Exchange by the business day or second business day after the call. Fail rate and waits are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for next-day securities settlement (fund delivers)
steps.description: When the fund delivers bonds rather than cash, the securities usually settle on the next business day through the custodian and the settlement depository, so the call stays pending overnight.

evidence.note: Margin must be exchanged by the second business day after the call. Share of securities deliveries and timing are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a failed delivery
steps.description: The associate works with the custodian and counterparty on why the delivery failed, such as wrong instructions, a cut-off missed or securities not available, and re-instructs or substitutes cash.

evidence.note: Common settlement exception handling. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large buy-side collateral team in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Check incoming collateral
steps.description: For calls the fund is owed, the associate checks the custodian report that the cash or securities arrived on time, in the agreed amount and are eligible after haircuts, and marks the call settled.

evidence.note: Eligible collateral and exchange deadlines. Shares and waits are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for next-day securities delivery (fund receives)
steps.description: When the counterparty delivers securities rather than cash, they usually arrive on the next business day, so the associate checks receipt the following morning.

evidence.note: Margin must be exchanged by the second business day after the call. Share of securities deliveries and timing are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chase missing or ineligible collateral
steps.description: The associate contacts the counterparty about collateral that has not arrived or is ineligible, agrees a replacement or a new value date and records the late delivery for counterparty credit review.

evidence.note: Common exception handling. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large buy-side collateral team in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Confirm settlement and update collateral records
steps.description: The associate marks the call settled, updates collateral held and posted by agreement and checks that the collateral system and custodian balances agree for that agreement.

error.defect_description: Balance not updated, so the next day's call is wrong.

evidence.note: Standard close-out of a call. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large buy-side collateral team in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Post collateral movements to the book of record
steps.description: An interface posts cash collateral movements, interest and securities pledges from the collateral system to the investment book of record for accounting and reconciliation.

error.defect_description: Mapping failure leaves a movement unposted until the cash reconciliation finds it.

evidence.note: Cash collateral pledged and received is accounted for as investment receivables and liabilities. Interface timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review daily margin activity and send the margin summary
steps.description: At the end of the day a senior associate reviews settled, pending and disputed calls, collateral posted and received and excess collateral, and sends the margin summary to TFM's liquidity team and counterparty credit risk.

control.basis: Daily reporting of margin and collateral positions to treasury and counterparty risk

evidence.note: FSB recommends margin call liquidity risk is part of governance and liquidity management. Per-call share of the daily review time is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Exposure break before calling
exceptions.description: A missing booking, late novation or stale price makes an agreement's exposure wrong; trade support or pricing must fix it before the call goes out.

exceptions.name: Margin dispute
exceptions.description: The counterparty disputes an outgoing call, or the fund questions an incoming one; the undisputed amount moves and the rest is reconciled trade by trade.

exceptions.name: Aged dispute escalation
exceptions.description: A dispute stays open beyond several business days and is escalated to senior staff, counterparty management and, for EU counterparties above EUR 15 million for 15 business days, regulatory reporting.

exceptions.name: Failed or late collateral delivery
exceptions.description: A delivery fails or incoming collateral is late, short or ineligible and must be chased, re-instructed or substituted.

exceptions.name: Large call on a volatile day
exceptions.description: An unusually large call needs TFM's liquidity and collateral principal to confirm which cash or securities to use.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the morning margin calculation to settled, recorded collateral included in the daily summary
benchmarks.population: Bilateral, repo and cleared margin calls at a large buy-side firm

evidence.note: Rules require exchange on or before the business day after the call (US swap dealers) or by the second business day (OSFI E-22). Percentiles are the author's estimate: calls exchanged by late morning, cash settling the same afternoon and about a quarter of deliveries in securities settling the next business day, with disputes and weekends in the tail.
Guideline E-22 paragraph 15.
Guideline E-22 paragraphs 31 to 33.
Article 15 of Delegated Regulation 149/2013.

benchmarks.unit: CAD cumulative across the eight largest Canadian public pension funds
benchmarks.population: Canada's Big Eight public pension funds

evidence.note: Bank of Canada Staff Analytical Note 2021-11.

pain_points.description: Disputes over trade populations and valuations need manual trade-by-trade reconciliation by email and file exchange and can stay open for days.

evidence.note: Regulation requires procedures for disputes unresolved after five business days, showing they are common enough to regulate.

pain_points.description: Exposure accuracy depends on upstream trade booking and pricing; a missing trade or stale price holds back the call or causes a dispute.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common dependencies.

pain_points.description: Volumes and amounts spike in volatile markets, compressing the time to check, select and deliver collateral while liquidity is under strain.

evidence.note: March 2020 margin calls peaked at about C$30 billion in one week across the Big Eight; FSB documents spikes in several episodes.

pain_points.description: Counterparties not on electronic messaging still exchange calls by email, adding re-keying and matching work.

evidence.note: Electronic messaging is used by most but not all firms that exchange margin.

sources.title: Liquidity Preparedness for Margin and Collateral Calls: Final report
sources.supports: Margin and collateral calls rose sharply and frequently in March 2020, Archegos, 2022 commodities and LDI episodes; recommendations on liquidity governance, stress testing, resilient operational and collateral management processes, sufficient liquid assets and regular interaction with counterparties and service providers

sources.title: Margin Manager (product page, formerly AcadiaSoft)

sources.title: Associate, Cash, Collateral & Settlements Operations (job posting)
sources.supports: Cash, collateral and settlements team at this organisation settles equities, bonds, repo, money markets, securities lending and FX; works with brokers, custodians and prime brokers; uses Bloomberg, SimCorp and affirmation platforms; escalates and resolves issues against market deadlines

assumptions: One case is one call in either direction on one agreement and value date; about 37% are calls the fund issues, 37% calls it receives, 19% cleared margin and 7% start with an exposure break. These shares are estimates.
Dispute rates (about 11% to 12% of bilateral calls) and resolution times are estimates; no public dispute statistics were opened because the ISDA survey pages could not be fetched.

Cycle time is measured from the morning when the overnight margin calculation is available, not from the close of the valuation date; about 25% of deliveries are assumed to be securities settling the next business day.

The team is the Cash, collateral and settlements team in the organisation file; the 10 collateral associates are assumed to spend about 60% of their time on call processing and the rest on agreement set-up, initial margin segregation, reconciliations and reporting.
The organisation file gives the collateral associate role a lower loaded cost than settlement senior associates; labour cost per call is driven by those figures.
Collateral optimisation decisions on what inventory is available are made in Total Fund Management outside this process; only approval of unusually large deliveries is shown.
Web search capacity ran out during research, so vendor process documentation and ISDA margin surveys could not be opened; affected numbers are tier C.
